newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland forecasts 4 pct growth in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland forecasts 4 pct growth in 1996/97.

text.p: Economic growth in the Australian state of Queensland was expected to be four percent in 1996/97, slightly above forecast national economic growth of 3.5 percent, deputy premier and Treasurer Joan Sheldon said.
"Gross state product for Queensland is expected to bounce back to four percent, half a percent above the national GDP," she said in a statement accompanying the state budget papers.
Sheldon said the current year's forecast growth compared with a "serious decline" last year in economic growth to only 2.2 percent, well below a projected 4.5 percent in GDP.

A major component of growth would come from a 1.5 percent increase in dwelling investment compared with a forecast national decline of three percent and an estimated 25 percent decline in Queensland in the previous year, Sheldon said.
Business investment was expected to grow by nine percent in 1996/97 against a national outlook of 14 percent, she said.
The unemployment rate was expected to remain at a year-average of about 9.3 percent but was expected to fall over the year to around nine percent by the June quarter next year.
"Further reductions in the unemployment rate will be constrained by relatively strong labour force growth," Sheldon said.
